description: Automation may improve vault quality but weaken human metacognition, comprehension, and knowledge-work ability.
topics: ["[[agent-cognition]]"]
source: TFT research corpus (00_inbox/heinrich/)

"To fully automate [metadata creation] is to outsource the very cognitive process that PKM seeks to enhance." Agent extraction, connection-finding, and synthesis may improve organization while human structuring, connection recognition, significance judgment, and encoding atrophy.

**Collector’s Fallacy variant:** Hidden agent processing makes the vault feel productive while comprehension remains shallow, enabling deeper collecting.

**Generation Effect bypass:** The generation effect (Slamecka & Graf, 1978) favors active generation over passive consumption. Agent translation/connections benefit the vault, not necessarily the human; approval may lack generative work. [[the generation effect requires active transformation not just storage]]

**Extended Mind decoupling:** [[cognitive offloading is the architectural foundation for vault design]] requires active mind-tool coupling. Agent processing without engagement makes the vault adjacent, not extended cognition; frictionless capture becomes disengagement. Mitigation may require human-in-the-loop synthesis, not only approval gates.

[[vibe notetaking is the emerging industry consensus for AI-native self-organization]] normalizes “dump everything, we organize it for you,” hiding lost generative work.

Counterargument: ars contexta preserves human judgment through agent proposals and human approval. Is curation active enough to prevent skill atrophy? Warning
